rules.title: Cartwright Act amendments (A.B. 325) on common pricing algorithms
rules.requirement: Businesses may not use or distribute a common pricing algorithm as part of an agreement to restrain trade. They also may not use or offer a common pricing algorithm while coercing users to adopt its price or commercial-term recommendations in California. A common pricing algorithm has two or more users and uses competitor data.
rules.key_value: Civil fines up to $1 million per violation; criminal fines up to $6 million for corporations and $1 million for individuals
rules.penalty: Civil fines of up to $1 million in cases brought by the Attorney General or a district attorney. Criminal fines are the greater of up to $6 million (corporations) or $1 million (individuals), or twice the gain or loss. Treble damages, injunctive relief and attorneys' fees remain available in private litigation.
rules.status_basis: Signed by Governor Newsom in October 2025; took effect January 1, 2026.

requires.name: common_pricing_algorithm
requires.text: A pricing algorithm is common if it has two or more users and uses competitor data in setting pricing or commercial terms

exempt_if.name: single_firm_algorithm
exempt_if.text: The law does not affect a business that uses proprietary algorithms utilizing only the business's own data

coverage.summary: Applies to users and distributors of pricing algorithms with two or more users that use competitor data, in any industry including apartment rentals.
coverage.exemptions_summary: Single-firm algorithms using only the business's own data are not covered.

rules.quoted_span: Businesses are expressly prohibited from using or distributing common pricing algorithms as part of an agreement to restrain trade.
